case_name: Govindappa and others v State of Karnataka
respondent:
State of Karnataka
Supreme Court of India

11  May  2010
Cr.A. No. 1469 of 2008
The Judgment was delivered by: P. Sathasivam, J.
1. This appeal is directed against the final judgment and order dated 04.10.2007 passed by the High Court of Karnataka at Bangalore in Criminal Appeal No. 2573 of 2006 whereby the High Court partly allowing the appeal acquitted Laxmibai - A-3, the mother of the appellants herein and Bhagirathi-A-5, the grandmother of appellants and affirming the sentence passed by the trial Court convicted A-1, A-2 and A-4, appellants herein, for offences under Section 498-A/34 IPC and Section 302/34 IPC.
2. The facts leading to the present appeal are as follows:
2.1. The deceased - Renuka, was married to appellant No.1 about 10 years prior to the date of the incident. As per the prosecution case, on 10.12.2005, at about 12 noon, the appellants herein, along with their mother and grandmother tried to pour kerosene oil and lit fire on the deceased and b
facts: The deceased - Renuka, was married to appellant No.1 about 10 years prior to the date of the incident.
On 10.12.2005, at about 12 noon, the appellants herein, along with their mother and grandmother tried to pour kerosene oil and lit fire on the deceased and because of that she raised hue and cry.

The Police Officer came to the hospital after 7 p.m. and taken the statement of the deceased which was written by Govindagowda Patil - PW-11, the neighbour, and FIR was registered at the police station at 7.15 p.m.
On 26.06.2006, the Fast Track Court, Bagalkot framed the charges against all the five accused persons under Sections 498A, 143, 147, 341, 302 read with S.149 IPC.
issues: Whether the Trial Court was justified in convicting the appellants-accused A-1, A-2, and A-4 for offences punishable under Section 498A, read with S.34 IPC and S.302 read with S.34 IPC?
Whether the sentence imposed upon the appellants-accused is justifiable?
Whether the High Court is right in confirming the conviction and sentence imposed on the appellants?
petitioner_arguments: The Trial Court accepted the evidence of eye-witnesses, namely, PW-3, PW-4, PW-5, PW-6 as well as Dr. Uma Kant PW-7 who treated Renuka, father of the deceased PW-9, one elderly person of the village PW-10 and Taluk Executive Magistrate PW-12 who had recorded the dying declaration of Renuka.

The Trial Court and the High Court committed an error in relying upon the dying declaration recorded by PW- 12 since PW-12 has neither taken the certificate from the Doctor nor asked any question to verify the mental condition of the deceased Renuka, particularly, when she suffered 100% burns as shown in the postmortem report.
respondent_arguments: The evidence of PW-7 coupled with PW-12 are acceptable and support the case of the prosecution.
Though, he also implicated A-3 and A-5 in the commission of offence but in the absence of further corroboration, the High Court has rightly acquitted them.
court_reasoning: We hold that the evidence of PW-7 coupled with PW-12 are acceptable and support the case of the prosecution.

Though this suggestion has been admitted by PW-7, the fact remains at the time of recording her statement PW-7 was satisfied that Renuka was in a fit condition and in a fit state of mind to make a statement.
His assertion that A-1 was holding Renuka also finds corroboration from the dying declaration Ex. P-9.
holding: We hold that the evidence of PW-7 coupled with PW-12 are acceptable and support the case of the prosecution.
The High Court has rightly accepted his testimony.
In other words, the evidence of PW-6 clearly proves the participation of A-1, A-2 and A-4 in the commission of offence.
